Central Nervous System
Anatomy
Diencephalon

The diencephalon is the part of the brain lying cranial to the midbrain, almost completely enclosed by the cerebrum, and its cavity forms the third ventricle. It is subdivided into five regions — the thalamus, hypothalamus, metathalamus, epithalamus, and subthalamus — each with distinct components and positions relative to the hypothalamic sulcus. The thalamus, the largest subdivision, is covered in detail: its external ends and surfaces, its internal division by the internal medullary lamina into anterior, medial, and lateral parts, and the specific nuclei housed within each part.

Complete Lesson Content

Diencephalon — Overview

The diencephalon is a part of the brain situated cranial to the midbrain and is more or less completely surrounded by the cerebrum. Its cavity forms the third ventricle.

Divisions of the Diencephalon

DivisionPosition / DescriptionComponents
ThalamusThe largest subdivision; ovoid gray matter mass lying dorsal to the hypothalamic sulcus—
HypothalamusPart of the diencephalon ventral to the hypothalamic sulcusOptic chiasma, hypophysis cerebri, posterior perforated substance, mamillary body
MetathalamusPresent at the caudal part of the thalamusMedial and lateral geniculate bodies
Epithalamus—Pineal gland, habenular nuclei and commissure, posterior commissure
SubthalamusGroup of gray matter nuclei between the thalamus and midbrain—

Thalamus — External Features

Ends

  • Anterior end: narrow end that projects forward, called the tubercle of thalamus; it forms the posterior boundary of the interventricular foramen.
  • Posterior end: expanded end known as the pulvinar; it overhangs the medial and lateral geniculate bodies.

Surfaces

SurfaceRelations
SuperiorRelated to the tela choroidea of the 3rd ventricle
InferiorAnteriorly fuses with the subthalamus; posteriorly related to the medial and lateral geniculate bodies
MedialForms the greater part of the lateral wall of the 3rd ventricle; connected to its fellow of the opposite side by the interthalamic adhesion
LateralRelated to the posterior limb of the internal capsule and the lentiform nucleus

Thalamus — Internal Parts

The internal medullary lamina is a vertical sheet of white fibers that traverses the thalamus, dividing it into three parts: the anterior, lateral, and medial parts.

Nuclei of the Thalamus

Thalamic partNuclei
Anterior partAnterior nucleus (collective term for the nuclei of this part)
Medial partLarge dorsomedial nucleus; small centromedian nucleus
Lateral part — dorsal divisionLateral dorsal, lateral posterior, and the pulvinar (craniocaudal order)
Lateral part — ventral divisionAnterior ventral, lateral ventral, and posterior ventral (craniocaudal order)

The lateral part of the thalamus is itself split into a dorsal and a ventral division, and each of these divisions is further subdivided into three named nuclei arranged front-to-back (craniocaudally).

Key Points / Quick Review

Diencephalon basics

  • Lies cranial to the midbrain, surrounded by the cerebrum
  • Its cavity forms the third ventricle
  • Five divisions: thalamus, hypothalamus, metathalamus, epithalamus, subthalamus

Hypothalamus vs. thalamus position

  • Thalamus lies dorsal to the hypothalamic sulcus
  • Hypothalamus lies ventral to the hypothalamic sulcus
  • Hypothalamus includes optic chiasma, hypophysis cerebri, posterior perforated substance, mamillary body

Metathalamus & epithalamus

  • Metathalamus = medial + lateral geniculate bodies (caudal thalamus)
  • Epithalamus = pineal gland, habenular nuclei/commissure, posterior commissure

Thalamic ends

  • Anterior end = tubercle of thalamus; bounds interventricular foramen posteriorly
  • Posterior end = pulvinar; overhangs geniculate bodies

Thalamic surfaces

  • Superior — tela choroidea of 3rd ventricle
  • Inferior — fuses with subthalamus anteriorly; geniculate bodies posteriorly
  • Medial — lateral wall of 3rd ventricle, joined by interthalamic adhesion
  • Lateral — internal capsule (posterior limb) and lentiform nucleus

Internal division & nuclei

  • Internal medullary lamina splits thalamus into anterior, medial, lateral parts
  • Anterior part → anterior nucleus
  • Medial part → dorsomedial + centromedian nuclei
  • Lateral part (dorsal) → lateral dorsal, lateral posterior, pulvinar
  • Lateral part (ventral) → anterior ventral, lateral ventral, posterior ventral
